name: Schezwan Pasta
steps: Remove the stems and most seeds from the dried chillies. Soak them in 100 ml hot water for 10 minutes. Blend the softened chillies with the soaking water, tomato paste, vinegar, half the garlic and ginger to a thick, smooth sauce. Wash and slice the peppers and carrot into thin, similar-sized strips; keep the spring onion greens separate.

Bring the remaining 3000 ml water to a rolling boil in a large pot. Add 6 g salt and the penne; stir and cook 1 minute less than the packet's al dente time, usually 9–11 minutes. Reserve 200 ml of cooking water, then drain. The pasta will finish cooking in the sauce.

Heat 20 ml oil in a wide pan over medium heat. Add the blended chilli mixture and stir continuously for 4–5 minutes until its raw garlic smell fades and the oil begins to separate around the edge. If it catches, add a spoonful of reserved pasta water. Set this cooked schezwan sauce aside.

Increase the heat to medium-high and add the remaining 20 ml oil. Stir-fry the carrot for 2 minutes, then the peppers and spring onion whites for another 2 minutes. Keep the vegetables bright and slightly crisp. Add the remaining garlic and ginger; stir for 30 seconds.

Return the cooked chilli sauce to the pan with the soy sauce and 100 ml reserved pasta water. Add the drained penne and toss over medium heat for 2 minutes until the sauce coats it evenly and the pasta is tender. Add a little more pasta water only if the pan looks dry.

Taste before adding up to the remaining 2 g salt; soy sauce also contributes salt. Divide between four bowls, scatter with spring onion greens and serve hot. The finished sauce should cling to the penne without pooling underneath.
tips: The heat level depends on the dried chillies. Remove all seeds or reduce their weight to 12 g for a milder family version. Use an eggless pasta and check that the soy sauce and vinegar are vegetarian.
notes: Quantities serve four adults. Check the doneness cues in each step and adjust seasoning to taste. Jain suitability depends on your household ingredient rules.
